_comment: AI GAME COMPANY cost-prevention policy (master prompt section 7). The orchestrator MUST load this before any agent call and refuse anything it forbids. Editing a false to true is a deliberate act with billing consequences.
_codex_writes_all_code_note: Set true on 2026-09-02 on the user's instruction: all coding is requested from Codex. Claude writes specifications onto TASKBOARD.json, reviews the resulting diff, and maintains config/docs; it does not author production code while this is true. Note the practical cost, which is not a policy question: the codex CLI is installed on the build PC and NOT in the Claude Code container, so Claude can only QUEUE work here - nothing lands until 'orchestrator team run' is executed on the PC.
_allow_gemini_design_note: Set true on 2026-09-02 because the user asked for Gemini to be integrated for design work, free of charge. FOUR limits, all of which belong in code and not just here. (1) A SEPARATE env var: GEMINI_API_KEY, deliberately not GOOGLE_API_KEY - that one stays on blocked_env_keys so nothing else in this project silently starts spending a Google key. (2) FREE MODELS ONLY: the adapter must refuse any model id not in gemini_free_tier_models. (3) NEVER ESCALATE: a 429/quota response degrades like on_codex_limit does - it must never retry against a paid tier or a billed project. (4) The key is a HUMAN_GATE (initial_gemini_login) and must never be committed, logged, or printed; presence may be recorded, the value never. Google's own pricing page (ai.google.dev) is blocked by this environment's egress proxy, so the free tier was NOT verified against a first-party source - which is exactly why the code must fail rather than assume.
_allow_codex_write_note: Set true on 2026-09-02 because the user asked for Codex to develop alongside Claude rather than only review. It runs 'codex exec --sandbox workspace-write', so its edits are confined to the repository, and teamwork.run_task additionally checks the resulting git diff against each task's declared file allowlist. It does NOT relax allow_openai_api_billing - this is still the subscription, not the paid API - and it grants no permission to commit or push: CLAUDE.md's rule that a human approves every commit is unchanged.
_auto_install_note: Section 43 permits installing components that cost nothing. Only free, no-login OSS tools are eligible. The installer verifies each package ID exists in the package manager before running it rather than assuming, per section 38. Accepting winget's standard source/package agreements for these OSS packages is covered by the user's explicit request to auto-install; every auto-accepted agreement is named in the install report.
_never_auto_install_note: unity: licence tier plus section 19's verified-build Baseline - a wrong editor version breaks the working APK pipeline. ollama_models / image models / 3d models: sections 4, 8 and 9 require verifying the licence of each specific model ID before use, and 'it is a Qwen' is explicitly not sufficient. comfyui: pulls model weights whose licences are unverified.
_blocked_env_keys_note: Section 7: the presence of one of these in the environment is NOT permission to use it. The orchestrator records presence only (never the value) and must not read it into any request while the matching allow_* flag is false.
_secrets_note: Section 3: never copy these into the project, never commit them, never print them to a log.
_on_codex_limit_note: Section 3: hitting the subscription limit must never auto-switch to billed API. Degrade, do not spend.
_human_gates_note: Section 37: everything NOT on this list should proceed automatically. Do not ask the user to confirm routine steps.
_build_verification_note: Section 18 and 32: all three must pass. Any one failing means BUILD_FAILED. Section 38 forbids reporting success without an APK actually on disk.
_retry_note: Section 31: after 5 attempts go to NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW. If the same error hash repeats, stop burning retries and move to root-cause analysis instead.
_allow_local_image_generation_note: Set true on 2026-09-02 because the user explicitly asked for a free image generation AI to be integrated. This is LOCAL only - it does not relax allow_cloud_ai_generation, which stays false, and no API is called. image_generation_models left never_auto_install for the same reason: the user asked. The section 8/9 gate still applies and was satisfied first - stable-diffusion-v1-5 is APPROVED in LICENSE_REGISTRY.json under CreativeML OpenRAIL-M, which permits commercial use, and the non-commercial Turbo variants were rejected on those grounds.
_comfyui_note: comfyui left never_auto_install on 2026-09-02 because the user asked for it explicitly. GPL-3.0, build-time only, never bundled into the APK. It does NOT make Qwen-Image runnable here - see the qwen-image entry in LICENSE_REGISTRY.json and HardwareProfile.image_model_fit().
_allow_hydra_proxy_note: HydraTeams (MIT, Pickle-Pixel) is a proxy that makes Claude Code Agent Teams model-agnostic: each teammate stays a full Claude Code instance with every tool, while its LLM is GPT, Gemini or a local model. It is built and present on this machine. Left FALSE because turning it on has three consequences that are policy decisions, not conveniences. (1) CREDENTIALS: upstream reads ~/.codex/auth.json automatically whenever OPENAI_API_KEY is unset, and --provider openai is the default - so the file on secrets_never_touched was read by accident rather than on purpose. The local copy is patched so that path requires --use-codex-auth, and no longer prints the plan type it decoded from the token; src/config.ts.orig is the original. (2) BILLING: --provider openai with an OPENAI_API_KEY is the paid API, which allow_openai_api_billing and on_codex_limit.escalate_to_paid_api both forbid. Only --provider chatgpt (the subscription, no metered cost) is compatible, and that is the mode that needs --use-codex-auth. The two limits meet here, which is why this is one flag and not two. (3) RULE 1: codex_writes_all_code names Codex as the implementer. Teammates on other models writing code is a change to that rule, and the user sets it.
